# Clipo

> Clipo is a screen recorder for product demos that runs entirely in the browser. Record a tab, a window or your whole screen, and Clipo turns it into a polished demo that zooms in on every click, smoothly and automatically. There is nothing to install and no browser extension. Credits are bought once and never expire. There is no subscription.

Most auto-zoom recorders need a desktop app for one operating system, or an extension from one browser's store. Clipo needs neither: open it in a tab, press record, and show your product the way you normally would. The zooms, the smooth cursor and the framing are done for you.

## How it works

1. Open Clipo in your browser, press record, and choose a tab, a window or your whole screen.
2. Show your product the way you normally would, talking over it if you like.
3. Stop recording. Clipo edits it for you: it zooms in on every click, trims the waiting and smooths the cursor.
4. Change anything you want on the timeline, then export the video in the size and format you need.

## What a creator gets

### Record in the browser
- Record a tab, a window or the whole screen, straight from the browser
- Record your microphone along with the screen, and the tab's or computer's sound where your browser allows it
- Nothing to install and no extension to approve
- Works in current desktop versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari, Brave and Opera, on macOS, Windows, Linux and ChromeOS

### Automatic zoom on every click
- The camera glides in on each click and eases back out once the result is on screen
- Nothing to mark or tag while recording
- Clipo suggests a zoom wherever a moment deserves one

### A cursor worth watching
- A shaky cursor path, redrawn smooth
- Arrow, ring or dot styles, with a glow, a trail and a ripple on every click

### Framed like a product shot
- Backgrounds, padding, rounded corners and a shadow, kept for every export

### Captions and steps
- Captions from your voice, timed and burned in, in the style you pick
- A step-by-step of the demo, written for you, ready for a help article or a voiceover script

### Private information stays private
- Blur, pixelate or cover an email, a key or a customer's name, for a moment or the whole recording

### An editor for every decision
- Every zoom, blur and caption sits on a timeline: drag it, retime it or delete it
- Point at an empty spot on the timeline and click to add your own zoom, blur or caption right there
- Choose how far each zoom goes in, and drag the frame on the preview to choose what it holds
- Trim, cursor settings and captions in the same place

### Output in the shape it has to land in
- MP4, WebM or GIF, from 720p up to 4K, at 24, 30 or 60fps
- 16:9 for product tours, 9:16 for Reels and Shorts, 1:1, and 4:5 for LinkedIn
- One-click presets for YouTube, Reels and Shorts, LinkedIn, X and GIF

## Pricing

- No subscription and nothing recurring. Credits are bought once and never expire
- New accounts start with 100 free credits
- Starter: Rs 199 for 250 credits
- Creator: Rs 499 for 700 credits
- Studio: Rs 999 for 1600 credits
- Analysing a recording and exporting a video are charged by the minute, and the cost is shown before anything is charged
- Payments are in Indian Rupees through Razorpay

## Who it is for

- Founders and product teams recording demos, launch videos and feature updates
- Support and customer success teams making walkthroughs
- Anyone who wants a polished, zoomed demo without installing a desktop recorder

## Frequently asked questions

### Do I need to install anything?
No. Clipo runs in a browser tab. There is no desktop app and no browser extension.

### Is Clipo free?
Every new account gets 100 free credits, enough to try it on real recordings. After that, credits come in one-time packs from Rs 199. There is no subscription.

### How long can a recording be?
Up to 30 minutes.

### Can I change what Clipo decides?
Yes. Every zoom, blur and caption can be moved, retimed, resized or deleted, and you can add your own anywhere on the timeline.

### How long are recordings kept?
Recordings are deleted automatically about a week after you last work on them, and you can delete one yourself at any time. Videos you have downloaded are yours to keep.

### Who owns the videos?
You do. You own your recordings and every video Clipo makes from them.

## Ownership and control

- Creators own their recordings and every video Clipo renders from them
- Recordings are uploaded securely and edited on Clipo's servers; the privacy policy has the details
- Recordings and their renders can be deleted at any time, and deleting removes the source file too
